name: Sardine
description: The sardine (Sardinops sagax) - in this 1956 baseline the ruling fish of the northern Benguela, grazing plankton in shoals so large they fed seabirds, seals, tuna and the biggest purse-seine fishery in Africa. Life-stage group of the source model's juvenile and adult sardine stanzas, measured separately and pooled here because the two stanzas form one population (juveniles take phytoplankton, adults add zooplankton). Under heavy fishing and the 1972 Benguela Nino warming the stock collapsed in the 1970s and never recovered - the regime shift this ecosystem is famous for.
